title: Cost Signal Observatory and Automated Serving Policies
creator: Amara Johnson
description: Goal: Build an internal Cost Signal Observatory (CSO) that centralizes route- and tenant-level cost signals and feeds an automated serving policy engine to apply dynamic batching/caching/quantization knobs. The CSO will enable PMs and SREs to: (1) detect regressions in token economics, (2) test policy-driven rollouts that optimize cost while maintaining quality & latency SLOs, and (3) provide a single source of truth for per-route serving recommendations. Scope: ingest per-request telemetry (tokens, seq_len, model_variant, latency, error), compute rolling cost-per-1k-tokens and cost-per-response, expose dashboards and alert rules, and prototype a policy engine that enforces safe quantization or batching thresholds with canary/A-B experiments.
objectives: Instrument and store per-route cost signals by Feb 1
Expose CSO dashboards and alerting for top 20 routes by Feb 10
Ship first automated serving policy: safe quantize-to-int8 canary for low-risk routes by Feb 28
Prove >=15% token-cost reduction across pilot tenants with <2% quality regression by Mar 15
success_metrics: No more than 2% drop in eval pass-rate vs baseline prompts
Policy decision latency <50ms added per request
Number of routes surfaced with actionable cost-saving recommendations >= 20
plan: Week 1: Schema + lightweight store (timeseries) + ingestion pipeline (events -> CSO) - ENG lead: Priya
Week 2: Compute signals (rolling cost, seq_len histograms, hot prefixes) + write dashboards - ENG/PM pairing
Week 3: Policy engine prototype (declarative rules + safe overrides) + integration tests
Week 4: Pilot with two internal tenants (console, embeddings) + monitor quality metrics
Week 5: Iterate on rollback heuristics and canary sizing; prepare runbook and postmortem template
tasks: ENG-2387: Ingest per-request telemetry to CSO (Priya) - In Review
ENG-2410: Rolling cost calculations and sequence length pipelines (Ravi) - In Progress

risks: Telemetry volume may increase storage costs — mitigation: 30d retention and sampling for low-traffic routes
Automated policies could degrade quality — mitigation: strict canary + automatic rollback on eval regressions
Cross-team dependency on runtime hooks (ENG runtime team) may delay enforcement integration
Latency overhead from policy checks — mitigation: cache decisions and precompute common routes
